item.title: [microsoft/playwright] v1.65.0
item.description:
## 🥟 Run tests with Bun
The test runner now runs under Bun. Bun transpiles your TypeScript test files itself, so Playwright does not use Babel or its compilation cache. Pass the `--bun` flag, because without it `bunx playwright test` runs on Node.js:
```bash bunx --bun playwright test ```
Our CI runs the test runner tests under Bun 1.4.3 on Linux. Some features work differently under Bun:
- There is no watch mode. UI mode does not run tests again when files change, and `--only-changed` does not follow imports. - Bun loads modules itself, so `--tsconfig` and the JSX options in `tsconfig.json` have no effect, and custom ESM loaders are not supported. - Stack traces do not include async frames, and API names do not include the class name: `click` instead of `locator.click`. This changes some step locations, step titles and error messages. - Console output of a test does not get into the trace and UI mode.

item.description:
## Breaking changes
- Changed the optional canvas and image decoding backend from `canvas` to `@napi-rs/canvas`. Install `@napi-rs/canvas` v1.0.13 or later in the v1.x series alongside jsdom; installing `canvas` alone no longer enables this support. The new backend provides prebuilt Skia binaries on supported platforms, and rendering and encoded image bytes can differ. Projects using native canvas objects or custom font registration should follow the canvas migration guidance. Added WebP serialization through `canvas.toDataURL` and `canvas.toBlob`. Fixed image loading to wait for decoding before firing `load`, discard obsolete source requests, avoid refetching when dimensions change, and prevent failed images from drawing stale contents. item.title: [pnpm/pnpm] pnpm 12.18 (v12.18.0)
item.description:
pnpm 12.18.0 packs, publishes, and installs packages with platform variants on pnpr registries. It also adds per-skill approval of agent skills and `pnpm store add` for offline installs from downloaded tarballs. Repeat installs and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` no longer read the `package.json` of unchanged workspace projects. The release fixes several peer dependency resolution bugs too.
### Minor Changes
#### Agent skills
- pnpm now names the link to a dependency's agent skill after the skill alone. A skill that the `@acme/kit` package ships in `skills/auth/` is linked as `.claude/skills/auth`, not `.claude/skills/pnpm-@acme+kit-auth`. The next install replaces links with the old names. pnpm lists the linked skills in a `# pnpm` block of each agent skill directory's `.gitignore` #17455.
When two approved packages ship a skill of the same name, or the name is already taken in an agent skill directory, pnpm links the skill as `pnpm-<package>-<skill>`. Before, the install failed.

item.description:
## 6.22.0 (2026-11-02)
The MongoDB Node.js team is pleased to announce version 6.22.0 of the `mongodb` package!
## Release Notes
> [!WARNING] > Node Driver versions from v6.11.0 before v6.22.0 (this release) and from v7.0.0 before v7.8.0 are affected by a security issue related to the use of the experimental timeoutMS feature where connection pool desynchronization after operation timeout can expose other users' data (CVE-2026-119179). Users are encouraged to discontinue the use of timeoutMS as soon as possible.
### `timeoutMS` is deprecated and now a no-op
> [!WARNING] > `timeoutMS` and `timeoutMode` are deprecated and have no effect starting in this release. They are still accepted and will not throw, but operations will no longer time out because of them. They are slated for removal in a future release.
Use the per-stage timeouts instead: `serverSelectionTimeoutMS`, `waitQueueTimeoutMS`, `socketTimeoutMS`, and `maxTimeMS` for server-side execution. ### Features

item.description:
## v0.35.0 — November 2, 2026
This release aligns request option handling, parameter validation and form serialization across Node and browser runtimes on the v0.x line, with some stricter validation, and moves v0.x CI onto Namespace runners.
## ⚠️ Breaking Changes & Deprecations
- **Parameter Depth Limit:** `params` nested deeper than 100 levels now reject with `ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE`. (**#11243**) - **Form Index Serialization:** Sparse arrays and non-canonical numeric form indexes, such as `01`, now serialize as keyed objects instead of being collapsed into arrays. (**#11243**) - **Native Proxy Agents:** On runtimes with native environment proxy support, agents that override native pool-management or TLS-session lifecycle hooks now reject with `ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE`. Use an agent constructed without `proxyEnv` for these configurations. Plain subclasses are still supported, and public type signatures are unchanged. (**#11243**)

item.title: [anomalyco/opentui] Release v0.8.0 (v0.8.0)
item.description:
Most of 0.8.0 makes each frame cheaper. In 0.7.0, every frame cleared and repainted the whole screen and compared every row with the terminal, even when only a spinner had moved. Now an unchanged frame paints nothing, and a frame with a small change repaints only the rows around it. In OpenCode, a frame with a spinner or a streamed line does about a twentieth of the cell operations it did.
ScrollBox now scrolls and follows new content in native code. Animations share one clock: before, an app with several animations could draw twice as many frames as the animations needed.
The native input parser is still opt-in. It now keeps a mouse wheel report that a slow link splits, which the default parser can type into the focused input as text. To try it, set `OTUI_NATIVE_INPUT_PARSER=1`, or pass `experimental_nativeInput: true` to the renderer.

item.description:
### Notable Changes
This release marks the transition of Node.js 26.x into Long Term Support (LTS) with the codename 'Lithium'. It will continue to receive updates through to the end of April 2029.
Other than updating metadata, such as the `process.release` object, to reflect that the release is LTS, no further changes from Node.js 26.12.1 are included.
If you are updating from an earlier Long Term Support release (e.g. Node.js 24 or 22 or earlier) please note that since Node.js 25 the official binaries for Linux are linked against libatomic, which may need to be installed separately depending on your Linux distribution.

item.title: [theMackabu/ant] v16.5.c41757b4.0
item.description:
> [!IMPORTANT] > This release includes fixes for several security issues in fetch, HTTP, TLS, DNS, the sandbox, WebAssembly, FFI, Buffer, and the package manager. Upgrading is recommended for all users.
We now have real threads in Ant. `worker_threads` and the web `Worker` now run on in-process isolates instead of child processes, with Node-compatible messaging, `MessageChannel`, `BroadcastChannel`, and cross-thread `navigator.locks`. The new `ant:isolate` module runs untrusted code under memory limits and timeouts. Several realms can now share one isolate, so `node:vm` contexts get their own intrinsics. Async functions now run in the JIT, async calls are up to 2x cheaper, and `return await` settles in the same tick as in Node.
This release also replaces the Zig package manager with one written in TypeScript on top of upm, which removes Zig from the build. `--watch` now runs on isolates, and the new `--hot` flag reloads changed modules in place. `node:dns` is rewritten, TLS and
... (truncated)

item.title: [fastapi/fastapi] 0.162.0
item.description:
Omitted `bool` and `bool | None` form fields now use their declared defaults or produce missing-field errors, consistent with other fields and Pydantic behavior. FastAPI no longer infers `False` for omitted booleans. This applies to individual form parameters, form models, and unions of form models.
Omitted boolean model fields are excluded from `model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`, and their defaults no longer count as submitted fields during union selection. Default factories and `validate_default` follow the usual rules.
For HTML checkboxes, declare a boolean with a default of `False`. See Boolean Form Fields.
### Breaking Changes
* 🐛 Restore default handling for omitted boolean form fields. PR #16605 by @tiangolo.
